title: Damage, Expiry and Market Return Claims
summary: Check every damage, expiry and market-return claim against batches, invoices, return notes and destruction proof, so finance credits only stock that really qualifies.

seo.title: Damage and Expiry Claims Reconciliation | VipraTech
seo.description: Validate distributor damage, expiry and market-return claims against batches, invoices, return notes and destruction proof before finance issues credit.

problem.intro: Brands take back damaged, near-expiry and expired stock from distributors and retailers, usually under a policy that caps returns as a share of sales and sets which batches and reasons qualify. Claims arrive with return notes, batch lists, photos and destruction certificates, and checking them against the original invoices takes days.

pain_points.title: Batches never sold to that distributor
pain_points.detail: Returned batch and invoice numbers often do not match what the distributor actually bought, and nobody cross-checks every line.

pain_points.title: Return caps applied by hand
pain_points.detail: Return allowances as a share of purchases, by period and category, are calculated in spreadsheets and applied inconsistently.

pain_points.title: Weak destruction and salvage proof
pain_points.detail: Destruction certificates and photos are missing, reused from earlier claims or do not match the quantities claimed.

pain_points.title: Saleable stock returned as damaged
pain_points.detail: Without checking expiry dates and reasons, saleable stock comes back as damaged and is credited at full value.

solution.overview: VipraTech reads each return claim with its return notes, batch lists, photos and destruction certificates, and checks every line against the original sales invoices: was this batch sold to this distributor, at what price, and is it within or past its shelf life as claimed. Your returns policy is configured as rules, including caps as a share of purchases and the reasons that qualify. Duplicates are checked across months, and lines that fail or lack proof go to an exception queue with the reason. Finance approves the credit note sheet, and every decision keeps its evidence.
capabilities: Matches returned batches and quantities to the original invoices to that distributor
Checks expiry dates and shelf life against the reason claimed
Applies return caps by period, category and distributor from your policy
Checks that destruction certificates and photos exist, match the claim and are not reused
Values each line at the right price, net of salvage where it applies
Exception queue with reason codes, and a credit note sheet for finance

workflow.title: Receive return claims
workflow.detail: Distributors send return claims with return notes, batch lists, photos and destruction certificates.

workflow.title: Normalise lines
workflow.detail: Each line is read into distributor, SKU, batch, quantity, reason and claimed value.

workflow.title: Trace to invoices
workflow.detail: Every batch is traced to the sales invoices to that distributor, with price and date.

workflow.title: Apply the returns policy
workflow.detail: Shelf life, qualifying reasons and return caps are checked, and the eligible value is recalculated.

workflow.title: Exception review
workflow.detail: Lines without proof, outside the cap or with a mismatched batch go to finance with the reason.

workflow.title: Approve and credit
workflow.detail: Finance approves the credit note sheet, and each distributor gets a line-by-line statement.

match_rules.logic: Every returned batch must trace to a sales invoice to the same distributor. The quantity is capped at what that invoice sold, less earlier returns.
Expiry returns must be past expiry or inside the near-expiry window on the claim date. Damage returns need a damage reason and proof.
Eligible returns for the period stay within the cap set as a share of the distributor's purchases, by category.
Destruction certificates and photos must exist where required, match the quantities and not repeat an image or certificate from an earlier claim.
Each line is valued at the invoiced price or the policy return price, net of salvage where it applies.

exception_codes.meaning: The batch was never invoiced to this distributor.
exception_codes.action: Reject, or ask where the stock was bought.

exception_codes.meaning: The claimed quantity is above what was sold, less earlier returns.
The batch still had shelf life beyond the return window.
exception_codes.action: Reject as saleable stock, or approve as an exception.

exception_codes.meaning: The claim takes returns past the policy cap for the period.
exception_codes.action: Approve up to the cap. The rest needs sign-off.

exception_codes.meaning: A photo or certificate matches one used in an earlier claim.
exception_codes.action: Hold and ask for fresh proof.

faqs.q: Our returns policy differs by category and channel. Can it handle that?
faqs.a: Yes. Caps, qualifying reasons and price rules are configured per category, channel and period, and the version valid for each claim is applied.

faqs.q: What if our invoices do not carry batch numbers?
faqs.a: The system matches on SKU, quantity and date instead and marks those matches as weaker, so finance can decide how much evidence it needs.
No. It checks documents and data. Where you run physical verification, its results can be added as evidence on each claim.

faqs.q: Is this the same system as your distributor claims settlement?
faqs.a: Yes. Every VipraTech workflow runs on one claims engine: the document reading, matching, review queue and audit trail are shared. For this workflow we set up your returns policy as versioned rules, along with your document templates and matching keys.
